hypothesis: Affordability terms appeared more often in campaign content and were salient to surveyed voters.
data_needed: content corpus + poll/exit poll + time series
candidate_variables: content share by week; issue priority; support by poll date
limitations: Association does not establish persuasion; content sample may be selective.

hypothesis: Campaign contact activity may be associated with turnout and support in areas with more outreach.
data_needed: Canvass/phone data, precinct results, turnout history
candidate_variables: contacts per registered voter; turnout change; vote-share change
limitations: Public contact data may be unavailable; contact allocation is not random.

hypothesis: Online reach and engagement rose alongside polling support and media attention.
data_needed: Time-stamped post metrics, poll dates, media counts
limitations: Time trends and virality do not prove causal effect.

hypothesis: Second and later preferences changed the primary result relative to first-choice totals.
data_needed: Official rounds and cast vote record
candidate_variables: transfer rates, inactive ballot rate, round-by-round share
limitations: Transfer behavior cannot be equated with endorsement effect.

hypothesis: Public matching funds and small contributions financed campaign operations.
data_needed: Candidate-level finance records and CFB program rules
candidate_variables: small-donor count/share; public funds; spending categories
limitations: Funding and support may reinforce each other; distinguish campaign vs independent spend.

hypothesis: Turnout and participation patterns differed by age/geography and influenced citywide outcomes.
data_needed: Election-district returns, voter registration, ACS context
candidate_variables: turnout by district; candidate share; changes from comparable cycles
limitations: Area-level demographics cannot identify individual voters or motives.

hypothesis: Support varied across boroughs and election districts and may have expanded over the campaign.
candidate_variables: vote share by geography and election stage
limitations: Use certified data and stable geography keys; avoid ecological fallacy.

hypothesis: Attention and opposition narratives intensified around campaign milestones.
limitations: Sentiment labels are subjective; attention can be positive, negative, or neutral.

hypothesis: Public coverage of biography and representation may have shaped discussion and visibility.
candidate_variables: share of coverage by theme; survey measures if available
limitations: Do not assume identity predicts an individual's vote.
